ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory FICA risk-based customer due diligence. All UBOs, directors, signatories, and material counterparties must be screened against: (i) the South African targeted financial sanctions list published by the Financial Intelligence Centre under POCDATARA; (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) the OFAC SDN List (mandatory as a precondition to any US FDA 510(k) client engagement); and (iv) licensed commercial PEP databases covering domestic and foreign politically exposed persons. Screening results must be documented and retained for at least 5 years. Any positive match or ambiguous-name result triggers enhanced due diligence and, where warranted, a Suspicious Transaction Report to the FIC.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC e-Services Portal (https://eservices.cipc.co.za) - Name Reservation module (Form CoR 9.4)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in the Latin script; a name may be submitted in any of the 11 official South African languages, but non-Latin scripts require an official Romanized transliteration. Standard commercial practice is an English name with the mandatory suffix '(Pty) Ltd'. The name must not be misleading, offensive, contra bonos mores, or falsely imply connection with the state, a regulated profession, a university, a financial-services provider, or a foreign regulator (in particular 'FDA', 'CE', or 'SAHPRA').
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank / Building Society / Insurance / Assurance / Financial Services Provider (FSCA consent required under Banks Act 94 of 1990 and FAIS Act 37 of 2002)
Medical Scheme / Medical Aid / Hospital (Council for Medical Schemes consent required)
Auditor / Accountant / Attorney / Advocate / Trust / Chartered (reserved to licensed professionals with regulator consent)
University / College / School (Department of Higher Education and Training consent required)
Government / State / National / Provincial / Municipal / Reserve (false official-status implication)
President / Minister / Commission / Board (official title misuse)
FDA / CE / SAHPRA / Medical (misleading suggestion of US FDA authorization, EU CE marking, or South African Health Products Regulatory Authority registration)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: CIPC reserves an approved name for 60 business days (approximately 84 calendar days). The applicant may apply once for a 20-business-day extension (approximately 28 calendar days) with payment of the prescribed extension fee. Upon refusal, CIPC issues written grounds; the applicant may file a written objection within 20 business days of the refusal, and may appeal an adverse objection decision to the Companies Tribunal within 40 business days of the decision (Companies Act s. 13; Companies Regulations 74-75). Filing up to 3 alternative names simultaneously is the standard mitigation strategy.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted with conditions: the company must maintain a physical street address in South Africa at which business communications and legal process may be received (Companies Act s. 23(3)); a post-office-box address alone is unlawful. A licensed serviced-office or virtual-office provider that supplies a physical street address, mail-receipt services, and regulatory-correspondence handling satisfies the requirement for this low-risk professional consulting entity, provided directors can physically access the premises and SARS/CIPC correspondence is retained and retrievable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approximately 10-15%). CIPC and SARS primarily verify commercial substance through annual returns, tax filings, and Beneficial Ownership Register filings. Unannounced physical inspection risk escalates if the BOR is incomplete, if FIC suspicious-transaction reporting is triggered, or if the FDA 510(k) / CE Mark advisory scope expands into distribution or brokerage of health products in South Africa, which would require SAHPRA licensing.

stage_2.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Employment and Labour – Occupational Health and Safety Directorate / Compensation Fund (no industrial manufacturing licence applies to an office-based professional-services company); SAHPRA would become the competent authority only if the company later physically imports or distributes medical devices.
stage_2.operating_license_title: No industrial operating permit required for ISIC 7490 regulatory consultancy; municipal Certificate of Occupancy and OHS Act workplace clearance are the operative compliance instruments; optional SAHPRA establishment licence (s22C of Medicines and Related Substances Act 101 of 1965) for future device handling.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) – Environmental Authorisation Directorate; local municipal Environmental Health Department
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no listed activity under the EIA Regulations 2014 (GN R327 Listing Notices 1–3) is triggered by office-based professional services; no Basic Assessment Report or full EIA scoping report required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOC emissions generated; office effluent limited to sanitary discharge under municipal sewerage by-laws; hazardous waste (batteries, e-waste, printer cartridges) must be segregated and removed by a registered waste transporter under the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008 (NEMWA); waste manifest and disposal certificates retained for 5 years.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); primary digital portal: SARS eFiling (https://efiling.sars.gov.za).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must first incorporate as a private company or register as an external company with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC). Thereafter apply for an Income Tax reference number through SARS eFiling using the CIPC registration certificate and SARS combined registration process for Income Tax, VAT, PAYE/UIF/SDL, and Customs. A South African responsible person or authorised representative may be required. For VAT, register for a VAT number if taxable supplies exceed R1,000,000 in any consecutive 12-month period (compulsory) or exceed R50,000 (voluntary). For export transactions, obtain a SARS Customs client code and, where applicable, an import/export code prior to executing zero-rated supplies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; resident companies are taxed on worldwide income, non-resident companies are taxed on South African-source income; a (Pty) Ltd is not a pass-through entity and is subject to corporate income tax at 27%.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box or pass-through election exists for a (Pty) Ltd. Entity classification follows the legal personality conferred by the Companies Act 71 of 2008. Statutory mechanics include VAT grouping election under section 50 of the VAT Act, annual accounting and basis of accounting elections, and the application of controlled foreign company rules and hybrid mismatch rules (sections 23M–23X of the Income Tax Act) where cross-border payments are involved.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration: taxable supplies exceed R1,000,000 in any consecutive 12-month period or realistic future projection; voluntary registration: taxable supplies exceed R50,000 per 12-month period.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API-mandated e-invoicing or digital stamping regime is currently imposed by SARS. VAT vendors must issue valid tax invoices with prescribed particulars, retain records for five years, and submit VAT201 returns electronically via eFiling. SARS is progressively modernising e-invoicing standards, but there is no immediate CTC/continuous transaction control mandate.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to the export of movable goods where the supplier exports the goods from South Africa under SARS customs supervision and retains the required documentary proof. Supplies of services to non-residents, including professional/regulatory consulting services, may qualify for zero-rating under VAT Act section 11(2)(l) where the services are not used in South Africa and satisfy the statutory export service conditions. Evidence must demonstrate that the goods left South Africa within the prescribed export period and that payment was received from abroad. Compliance with the VAT export rules is required to claim input tax deductions and refunds.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign-currency bank receipt evidencing payment repatriation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Invalid or unsupported zero-rating is treated as a taxable supply at 15%, resulting in assessment, output tax, interest, and understatement penalties (up to 50%–150% depending on conduct), additional tax for deliberate non-compliance, and possible criminal prosecution for fraud. SARS can retrospectively claw back refunds and apply penalties for false declarations or failure to meet documentary and export-proceeds remittance requirements.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), acting through its Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), which administers the Currency and Exchanges Manual for South Africa (Issue 1/2023 and subsequent amendments). All exchange control functions are delegated to authorised dealers, being Category I commercial banks, which execute, verify, and report cross-border transactions under the SARB mandate.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Africa operates a partially regulated exchange-control regime. Current-account payments for professional and consulting services are broadly convertible and remittable, provided that supporting documentation (service agreement, tax invoice, and proof of service delivery) is presented to the authorised dealer and the applicable Balance of Payments (BOP) purpose code is accurately captured. Capital-account transactions, including inbound equity subscription, shareholder loans, and outward investment, are subject to SARB FinSurv general approvals or individual approvals and must be routed through normal banking channels with an executed SARB Form A (Inward Transfer of Funds) or Form B (Outward Transfer of Funds), as applicable. Profit and dividend remittances to non-resident shareholders are lawful once the underlying share capital or shareholder funding was originally introduced into South Africa through an authorised dealer and recorded on the company's Annexure 'A' (listing of foreign equity and loan funding). Any such remittance is subject to a 20% dividends withholding tax (DWT) under the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962, with no exchange-control conversion limit on the Rand amount to be repatriated. No surrender of services-export receipts at a fixed percentage is imposed, although all foreign-currency receipts must be converted to Rand on receipt unless an authorised-dealer-approved foreign-currency account is maintained.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Chapter VI of the SARB Currency and Exchanges Manual, proceeds of exported services, including MedTech regulatory consulting fees, must be received in full within 180 days from the date of the invoice or, where a service contract specifies milestones, from the date of completion of the milestone. Receipts in USD, EUR, GBP, or other foreign currency must be credited to the resident company's Rand-denominated operational account and converted to ZAR immediately upon receipt, unless the authorised dealer has granted express approval to maintain a foreign-currency account (FCA) under a general or specific approval. There is no fixed mandatory surrender ratio for services; however, 100% of the Rand-equivalent of all export proceeds must be accounted for to the bank via the BOP reporting system, and the bank must be furnished with the supporting invoice and inward SWIFT reference. Failure to receive proceeds within 180 days constitutes an exchange-control contravention requiring a FinSurv application for extension or condonation. For consulting engagements, advance payments received as deposits are classified as current-account receipts and must be declared as such, with subsequent offsets against invoices recorded consistently.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility with strict legal limitations. Non-bank offshore electronic money institutions (EMIs) and payment fintechs are not licensed as banks under the Banks Act 94 of 1990 and cannot lawfully accept deposits or offer full banking services in South Africa without either being registered as a South African bank or obtaining an approval as an authorised payment system participant under the National Payment System Act 78 of 1998 (through Bankserv/PASA membership) and, where applicable, an FSP licence under the FAIS Act 37 of 2002. Offshore EMIs (e.g., Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex) may be used as secondary convenience rails for inbound client fee collection in foreign markets, but SA-resident treasury funds must remain with a domestic authorised dealer to preserve exchange-control traceability, BOP reporting, and the Annexure 'A' capital chain. Relying on an offshore EMI as the principal treasury account is not viable for a Pty Ltd established for export consulting, because SARB record-keeping for future dividend repatriation, SARS audit trails, and bank anti-money-laundering (FICA) compliance would be rendered incomplete.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: FICA (Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001) and the banks' internal KYC policies mandate identification and verification of all natural-person directors, authorised signatories, and ultimate beneficial owners of a private company. In standard practice, at least one director or an authorised executive (with a valid mandate resolution) must physically attend a branch interview for first-time corporate account opening, particularly for foreign-owned entities. All Tier-1 banks permit partially digital onboarding for low-risk entities where the directors are South African tax residents and are verified via biometric e-LD verification; however, for a South African company whose ultimate beneficial owners are non-residents, the compliance teams typically require physical appearance of a director or a fully notarised and apostilled ID/passport package coupled with a live bank-verified video interview. The appointment of a local public officer or a resident non-executive director materially increases onboarding speed and reduces the risk of refusal.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate Beneficial Ownership (UBO) disclosure for a foreign-owned Pty Ltd with opaque shareholder chains
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CIPC Beneficial Ownership (COB) declaration form, duly certified shareholders register, Memorandum of Incorporation, notarised passports or national IDs of all ultimate natural persons, apostilled certificate of incorporation / good standing of each intermediate holding entity, and a signed UBO structure chart, all certified within 3 months of submission.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of Funds and source of wealth for inbound equity or intercompany funding injection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed subscription- or loan-agreement evidencing the inward transfer, remitting bank's reference details, six months of bank statements of the remitter, payroll or audited financial statements proving accumulation of funds, tax clearance of the foreign remitter or an equivalent tax authority confirmation, and a sworn legal affidavit explaining the pathway of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between declared business scope (FDA/CE advisory) and anticipated transaction flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Service agreements with foreign clients, export invoices, proof of professional indemnity insurance, company website and credentials substantiating regulatory advisory practice, and a 12-month cash-flow projection listing expected jurisdictions, average ticket sizes, and monthly wire frequencies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FATCA/CRS classification and SARS compliance of non-resident shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed FATCA/CRS self-certification (W-8BENE or CRS CFC), SARS income tax reference number of the Pty Ltd and its tax compliance status pin, provisional tax returns, and an annual financial statements history demonstrating no unresolved SARS debt.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media or sanctions screening hit on a director, shareholder, or counterparty
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Statutory declaration on Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) status, corroborating CV and source-of-wealth evidence, independent police clearance certificates for all directors, jurisdictional counsel opinion on sanctions exposure, and transactional documents evidencing no dealings with prohibited persons or sanctioned jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Failure to provide valid banking-mandate documentation for foreign resident signatories
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original or notarised board resolution appointing signatories, certified passport copies, proof of residential address (utility bill or notarised lease), issued foreign identity verification, and an FICA-compliant customer information sheet completed in the presence of the banker.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or shareholder-loan funding must be transmitted from the non-resident shareholder's foreign bank via SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for interbank settlement) to the authorised dealer in South Africa, with the beneficiary identified exactly as 'ZA Pty Ltd', and the SARB BOP purpose code '408' (equity subscription) or '410' (intercompany loan) stated in the SWIFT field 70/information. The authorised dealer will require a physically or digitally signed SARB Form A, certified board resolution, subscription or loan agreement, the shareholder register update, and the remitter bank's confirmation. Only funds thus recorded on Annexure 'A' qualify for later constitution-based dividend repatriation. For unrelated third-party clients paying for consultancy services, the proper inward purpose code is '415' (services rendered by residents to non-residents); the payment must be accompanied by an invoice reference in the SWIFT narrative and must be reported by the receiving bank as a current-account receipt convertible to ZAR without SARB approval.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: All outbound trade settlements and operational payments are routed through the authorised dealer using SWIFT MT103 (single customer credit transfer) or MT202 (for higher-value interbank settlement), with the applicable SARB BOP purpose code entered in field 72 or field 70 narrative. For services-related disbursements such as subcontracting fees to foreign laboratories and testing houses, purpose code '414' (services rendered by non-residents to residents) or '416' (manufacturing services) applies, while dividend remittances to non-residents use code '472'. For larger procurement contracts with overseas contract research organisations, a commercial letter of credit under UCP 600 may be established, with the issuing bank sending an SWIFT MT700 advice to the beneficiary's bank and settlement executed via MT202/MT103; documentary requirements (commercial invoice, certificate of service completion, inspection certificate) must mirror the underlying contract. All SARB records and underlying documentation must be retained for five years, and any outbound MT103 to a restricted or OFAC/UN-sanctioned jurisdiction is automatically blocked by bank system filters.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable Forward Exchange Contracts (FECs) with an authorised dealer, permitted for genuine commercial exposures of up to 12 months and renewable on evidence of an underlying foreign-currency invoice or contract; must be concluded within the ZAR/USD or ZAR/EUR interbank regime.

Cross-currency swaps and currency exchange agreements, available with authorised dealers for the hedging of multi-year service contracts, provided the notional is matched to actual expected foreign-currency receipts or disbursements.

Plain-vanilla FX options and zero-premium option collars, permitted for the hedging of a confirmed export-services income stream, subject to documenting the underlying exposure to the authorised dealer.

SARB-general-approval forward cover for expected but not yet invoiced export proceeds (sale proceeds cover), which may be taken out within prescribed parameters and only with an underlying service contract.

Offshore Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) are not permitted for South African resident corporates and require explicit FinSurv approval, which is rarely granted to a consulting entity; hence NDFs are excluded from permissible instruments.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023 (historically 28%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Corporation (SBC) progressive rates under s 12E for qualifying Pty Ltd with turnover below ZAR 20 million: 0% up to ZAR 95,000; 7% on ZAR 95,001-385,000; 21% above ZAR 385,000. Section 11D R&D additional 20% deduction (total 120%) for years of assessment commencing on or after 1 January 2024; s 12C accelerated depreciation for plant and machinery; general s 11(a) deductions; foreign tax credits under s 6quat for DTA jurisdictions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite carry-forward with no expiry; annual set-off capped at 80% of taxable income computed before the loss set-off for years of assessment commencing on or after 1 April 2022

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 - Income Tax Return for Companies, filed electronically via SARS eFiling; provisional payments use the IRP6 return on eFiling
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual ITR14 return; two compulsory provisional (IRP6) payments per year of assessment plus one voluntary top-up payment
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: ITR14 must be filed within 12 months after the end of the company's year of assessment (SARS issues individual eFiling deadlines). IRP6: first payment within 6 months of the start of the year of assessment; second payment on or before the last business day of the year of assessment; voluntary top-up within 6 months after year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SARS income tax reference number and Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) registration number of the Pty Ltd.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SA resident Pty Ltd is the registered taxpayer; non-resident shareholders appear only on the separate Dividends Tax declaration (DTD.1), not on ITR14.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross income from FDA 510(k) consulting and CE Mark regulatory services, including management, engineering, and documentation fees derived from both local and foreign clients.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report global gross income on the SA return; a non-resident parent or affiliate must not be substituted as filer. Cross-border service fees to a non-resident connected person must be reported in the transfer pricing schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Taxable income and assessed loss lines
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable income after deductions, s 11D R&D claims, and set-off of assessed losses brought forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss set-off is limited to 80% of taxable income before the set-off. A foreign-controlled Pty Ltd cannot attribute losses to the non-resident shareholder.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section 11D research and development deduction line
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Additional deduction for qualifying scientific or technological R&D, requiring a pre-approval letter from the Department of Science and Innovation (DSI).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: FDA 510(k) and CE regulatory consulting is generally non-qualifying administrative work; claim only for true clinical or technical feasibility studies conducted in SA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of all connected-person transactions with non-residents, including intercompany fees, management charges, loans, and IP royalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No statutory de-minimis threshold applies under s 31 of the Income Tax Act; contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation should be retained for transactions exceeding ZAR 5 million in aggregate per annum.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declarations for Dividends Tax (20%), interest WHT (15%), and royalty WHT (15%) on payments to non-residents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withhold before payment and remit to SARS within 30 days of payment; reduced treaty rates apply only after the non-resident delivers the prescribed declaration and a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: SARS administrative non-compliance penalty (ANP) of up to ZAR 250 per day for late filing (for turnover above ZAR 10 million: greater of ZAR 250 per day or 0.5% of tax payable); 10% late-payment penalty plus interest at the prescribed rate (repo rate plus 7%) on unpaid tax; understatement penalties of 10%-150% of the shortfall (200% for repeat behaviour within 5 years) under s 223 of the Tax Administration Act.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% Dividends Tax on dividends declared and paid to non-resident beneficial owners; the Pty Ltd withholds and pays SARS by the last day of the month following the dividend declaration.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, the non-resident shareholder must furnish the Pty Ltd with a completed declaration and undertaking form (DTD.1(a)), supported by a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by its home tax authority. The company then withholds at the reduced treaty rate (commonly 0%-10%, e.g., 5% for substantial shareholdings under many SA DTAs). All declarations and TRCs must be retained for 5 years and produced on SARS demand.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: 15% statutory WHT, typically reduced to 0%-10% under SA DTAs. Royalties: 15% statutory WHT on IP and know-how payments, commonly reduced to 10%-12% under treaties (e.g., 12% under the SA-US DTA). Reduced rates require prescribed declarations (DTR.02 for interest, DTR.03 for royalties) plus a valid TRC.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory monetary threshold under s 31 of the Income Tax Act, but SARS transfer pricing review guidelines require contemporaneous Local File and Master File documentation for cross-border connected-person transactions exceeding approximately ZAR 5,000,000 in aggregate per annum; a Country-by-Country (CbC) report notification applies to multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least ZAR 10,000,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Africa has no Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations statute, but substance is mandatorily evidenced through: (i) Place of Effective Management (POEM) in s 1 of the Income Tax Act determining tax residence; (ii) CFC attribution under s 9D for offshore subsidiaries; (iii) arm's-length recharacterization of sham arrangements under s 31; and (iv) general anti-avoidance rules in ss 80A-80L. A Pty Ltd must demonstrate local managerial decision-making, qualified operational staff, physical office facilities, and SA operating bank accounts; a substance-less shell may be disregarded.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting offshore FDA/CE consulting fees from gross income, parking revenue in foreign nominee bank accounts, issuing false invoices, or fabricating deductions and expenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Understatement penalty of 150% of the tax shortfall for intentional tax evasion (200% for a repeat case within 5 years); 10% late-payment penalty; prescribed-rate interest; criminal conviction under ss 234-235 of the Tax Administration Act with a fine of up to ZAR 1,000,000 and/or imprisonment for up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers are jointly and severally liable under TAA s 155(1) where the company's failure to pay tax is attributable to fraud or gross negligence; SARS may obtain asset preservation orders under s 163 and court-imposed travel interdictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Pty Ltd as a nominee shell without staff, office, or management substance to divert US and EU client fees offshore or to obtain treaty benefits improperly.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR invalidation under ss 80A-80L; s 31 arm's-length recharacterization and transfer pricing adjustments; 75% understatement penalty for impermissible avoidance arrangements; denial of DTA relief; potential FIC adverse findings and bank de-risking.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face joint and several liability for the company's resultant tax debts under TAA s 155, plus sequestration and personal asset attachment in serious cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold Dividends, Interest, Royalties, or PAYE
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends to a non-resident shareholder without 20% Dividends Tax, paying interest or royalties without 15% WHT, or misclassifying employees as independent contractors to avoid PAYE.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS recovers the unwithheld tax from the Pty Ltd, plus a 10% penalty and interest; additional understatement penalties of 50%-150%; dividends tax non-compliance attracts criminal prosecution under the Tax Administration Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under TAA ss 155-156, directors are personally and severally liable for unwithheld employee taxes and withholding taxes; the corporate veil is pierced as a matter of statute.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the consultancy to move client funds through non-SACU high-risk corridors, failing to file annual Risk and Compliance Returns, or facilitating third-party payments without beneficial ownership records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FIC Act administrative fines of up to ZAR 10,000,000 per contravention for accountable institutions; money laundering under the Prevention of Organised Crime Act carries imprisonment of up to 15 years; assets are subject to forfeiture.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior managers bear personal criminal liability, travel restrictions, and civil restitution; personal and corporate assets may be frozen under POCA restraint and forfeiture orders.
